claim: Liver progenitor cells can differentiate toward both hepatocyte and biliary cell fates.
source: The progenitor cells of the developing liver can differentiate toward both hepatocyte and biliary cell fates.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a foundational concept.

claim: TGFβ and Notch signaling have established roles in liver progenitor fate specification.
source: In addition to the established roles of TGFβ and Notch signaling in this fate specification process, there is increasing evidence that liver progenitors are sensitive to mechanical cues.
evidence: The manuscript states these roles are 'established', indicating prior knowledge from the field.

claim: Liver progenitors are sensitive to mechanical cues.
source: In addition to the established roles of TGFβ and Notch signaling in this fate specification process, there is increasing evidence that liver progenitors are sensitive to mechanical cues.
evidence: The manuscript cites 'increasing evidence' suggesting this is supported by prior research.

claim: Biliary differentiation occurs at the periphery of circular microarrayed patterns.
source: In these defined circular geometries, we observed biliary differentiation at the periphery and hepatocytic differentiation in the center.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Hepatocytic differentiation occurs in the center of circular microarrayed patterns.
source: In these defined circular geometries, we observed biliary differentiation at the periphery and hepatocytic differentiation in the center.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Substantial mechanical stresses are present at the periphery of microarrayed patterns, coincident with maximal biliary differentiation.
source: Parallel measurements obtained by traction force microscopy showed substantial stresses at the periphery, coincident with maximal biliary differentiation.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by TFM data in Figure 4.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on Notch signaling.
source: We investigated the impact of downstream signaling, showing that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent not only on Notch and TGFβ but also E-cadherin, myosin-mediated cell contractility, and ERK.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by GSI inhibitor experiments in Figure 2.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on TGFβ signaling.
source: We investigated the impact of downstream signaling, showing that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent not only on Notch and TGFβ but also E-cadherin, myosin-mediated cell contractility, and ERK.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by SB-431542 inhibitor experiments in Figure 3.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on E-cadherin.
source: We investigated the impact of downstream signaling, showing that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent not only on Notch and TGFβ but also E-cadherin, myosin-mediated cell contractility, and ERK.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by DECMA antibody experiments in Figure 3.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on myosin-mediated cell contractility.
source: We investigated the impact of downstream signaling, showing that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent not only on Notch and TGFβ but also E-cadherin, myosin-mediated cell contractility, and ERK.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by blebbistatin experiments in Figure 5.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on ERK signaling.
source: We investigated the impact of downstream signaling, showing that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent not only on Notch and TGFβ but also E-cadherin, myosin-mediated cell contractility, and ERK.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by FR180204 inhibitor experiments in Figure 6.

claim: Differentiation of liver progenitors toward a hepatocytic fate is guided chiefly by signaling through Wnt, HGF, and FGF.
source: While differentiation of liver progenitors toward a hepatocytic fate is guided chiefly by signaling through Wnt, HGF, and FGF (Micsenyi et al., 2004; Berg et al., 2007; Schmidt et al., 1995), biliary fate is regulated by Notch and TGFβ signaling (Kodama et al., 2004; Clotman et al., 2005; Zong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Biliary fate is regulated by Notch and TGFβ signaling.
source: While differentiation of liver progenitors toward a hepatocytic fate is guided chiefly by signaling through Wnt, HGF, and FGF (Micsenyi et al., 2004; Berg et al., 2007; Schmidt et al., 1995), biliary fate is regulated by Notch and TGFβ signaling (Kodama et al., 2004; Clotman et al., 2005; Zong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: A gradient of TGFβ activity caused in part by expression of TGFβR2 and TGFβR3 in the periportal region leads to differentiation of progenitors toward a biliary epithelial fate.
source: Specifically, a gradient of TGFβ activity caused in part by expression of TGFβR2 and TGFβR3 in the periportal region leads to differentiation of progenitors toward a biliary epithelial fate (Clotman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Mutations in the ligand JAG1 or receptor NOTCH2 are associated with bile duct paucity and cholestasis in patients with Alagille syndrome.
source: In patients with Alagille syndrome, mutations in the ligand JAG1 or receptor NOTCH2 are associated with bile duct paucity and cholestasis (Li et al., 1997; Oda et al., 1997; McDaniell et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Deletion of the Notch effector Rbpj results in reduction of biliary fate and abnormal tubulogenesis.
source: Zong et al. further underlined the importance of Notch in particular for both biliary cell fate and morphogenesis by showing that deletion of the Notch effector Rbpj results in reduction of both biliary fate and abnormal tubulogenesis (Zong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: TGFβ-induced biliary differentiation of liver progenitor cells is coordinated by both substrate stiffness and matrix context and is further correlated with cell contractility.
source: Using combinatorial extracellular matrix (ECM) protein arrays, we showed that TGFβ-induced biliary differentiation of liver progenitor cells is coordinated by both substrate stiffness and matrix context and is further correlated with cell contractility (Kourouklis et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: YAP has been shown to regulate both Notch signaling and TGFβ in liver cells.
source: This is particularly interesting in the context of liver progenitor fate specification because YAP has been shown to regulate both Notch signaling and TGFβ in liver cells (Yimlamai et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: OPN+ cells are located at the periphery of patterns while ALB+ cells are located centrally.
source: Within these defined multicellular geometries, we observed OPN+ cells at the periphery of patterns while ALB+ cells were located centrally (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling data in Figure 1A.

claim: Counts of OPN+ cells peaked at the periphery and increased with the presentation of Notch ligands, particularly DLL4.
source: Counts of cells that were OPN+ peaked at the periphery and increased with the presentation of Notch ligands, particularly DLL4 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1B.

claim: ALB+ cells indicated central localization and only moderate induction by ligand in the center of patterns.
source: However, counts of cells that were ALB+ cells indicated central localization and only moderate induction by ligand in the center of patterns (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1C.

claim: SOX9-expressing cells are located at the periphery while HNF4A-expressing cells are central.
source: Evaluation of the expression of the biliary transcription factor SOX9 and hepatocytic transcription factor HNF4A revealed segregation similar to that of OPN and ALB (Figure 1D). Specifically, SOX9-expressing cells were at the periphery while HNF4A-expressing cells were central.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 1D.

claim: Biliary differentiation remains confined to the periphery independent of pattern size (300 µm, 600 µm, and 1000 µm diameters).
source: Quantification of peak OPN+ cell counts on these pattern sizes indicated that biliary differentiation remained confined to the periphery independent of pattern size (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Culture on 4 kPa substrates decreases counts of peripheral OPN+ cells compared to 30 kPa substrates.
source: Prompted by previous experiments which showed that liver progenitor differentiation is sensitive to substrate stiffness (Kourouklis et al., 2016), we also evaluated progenitor differentiation on soft (4 kPa) rather than stiff (30 kPa) substrates, observing decreased counts of peripheral OPN+ cells and similar responsiveness to GSI (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Soft substrates (4 kPa) reduce peripheral SOX9 expression compared to stiff substrates (30 kPa).
source: We also evaluated expression of SOX9 and HNF4A, observing reduction in peripheral SOX9 expression and an increase in central HNF4A expression on soft substrates compared to stiff (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 2C.

claim: Soft substrates (4 kPa) increase central HNF4A expression compared to stiff substrates (30 kPa).
source: We also evaluated expression of SOX9 and HNF4A, observing reduction in peripheral SOX9 expression and an increase in central HNF4A expression on soft substrates compared to stiff (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 2C.

claim: Jag1, Dll1, and Notch2 mRNA show peripheral localization on stiff (30 kPa) substrates.
source: When used to detect mRNA in arrayed patterns fabricated on stiff (30 kPa) substrates, we observed peripheral localization of Jag1, Dll1, and Notch2 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization in Figure 2E.

claim: Presentation of DLL4 induces an increase in centrally-located cells expressing mRNA for Jag1, Dll1, and Notch2 on stiff (30 kPa) substrates.
source: Presentation of the ligand DLL4 induced rearrangement of this expression pattern, specifically causing an increase in centrally-located cells expressing mRNA for each gene.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization in Figure 2E.

claim: On soft (4 kPa) substrates, ligand-induced central expression of Jag1 and Notch2 is lost.
source: On soft (4 kPa) substrates, we observed similar mRNA expression for cells presented with IgG but no longer observed ligand-induced central expression for Jag1 and Notch2.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization in Figure 2E.

claim: The responsiveness of liver progenitors to Notch ligand is enhanced by stiffer substrates.
source: This loss of ligand-induced central expression on soft substrates suggests that the responsiveness of liver progenitors to Notch ligand is enhanced by stiffer substrates.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of differential ligand response on different substrate stiffnesses.

claim: Segregation of liver progenitor fates is dependent on both Notch signaling and substrate stiffness.
source: Collectively, these data show that segregation of liver progenitor fates is dependent on both Notch signaling and substrate stiffness.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Treatment with SB-431542 reduces peripheral OPN+ cell counts.
source: Treatment with SB-431542 reduced the peripheral count of OPN+ cells while increasing central expression of HNF4A (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 3A.

claim: Treatment with SB-431542 increases central expression of HNF4A.
source: Treatment with SB-431542 reduced the peripheral count of OPN+ cells while increasing central expression of HNF4A (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 3A.

claim: Treatment with TGFβ1 increases counts of OPN+ cells uniformly across the patterns irrespective of ligand presented.
source: In contrast, treatment with TGFβ1 increased counts of OPN+ cells uniformly across the patterns irrespective of ligand presented (Figure 3A and B), in agreement with previous efforts showing uniform induction of OPN on patterns of smaller diameter (150 µm) (Kourouklis et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling and quantification in Figure 3A and B.

claim: TGFβ1 treatment results in loss of cell–cell junctional interactions.
source: Interestingly, we observed loss of cell–cell junctional interactions in cells treated with TGFβ1, which is thought to be a consequence of inhibition of E-cadherin expression by the Snail family of transcription factors (Cano et al., 2000; Vincent et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Loss of cell–cell junctional interactions with TGFβ1 treatment is thought to be a consequence of inhibition of E-cadherin expression by the Snail family of transcription factors.
source: Interestingly, we observed loss of cell–cell junctional interactions in cells treated with TGFβ1, which is thought to be a consequence of inhibition of E-cadherin expression by the Snail family of transcription factors (Cano et al., 2000; Vincent et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Treatment with DECMA (functional antibody against E-cadherin) results in differential responsiveness to control IgG and DLL4 presentation.
source: In contrast with our observations following treatment with TGFβ1, we observed differential responsiveness to control IgG and DLL4 presentation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 3B.

claim: Presentation of DLL4 to cells treated with DECMA results in uniform induction of OPN+ cells across the patterns.
source: Specifically, presentation of DLL4 to cells treated with DECMA resulted in uniform induction of OPN+ cells across the patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 3B.

claim: Jag1 and Notch2 remain expressed at the periphery after SB-431542 treatment.
source: Last, although inhibition of TGFβ by treatment with SB-431542 reduced OPN+ cell counts, mRNA in situ hybridization of cultures treated with SB-431542 indicated that both Jag1 and Notch2 remain expressed at the periphery (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization in Figure 3C.

claim: SB-431542 treatment reduces expression of both Jag1 and Notch2 in centrally-located cells presented with DLL4.
source: However, SB-4315412 treatment reduced expression of both Jag1 and Notch2 in centrally-located cells presented with DLL4 (Figure 3C), which we had previously observed in untreated cultures (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization in Figure 3C.

claim: TGFβ only partially regulates fate segregation.
source: These data therefore demonstrate that TGFβ only partially regulates fate segregation and that these effects are additionally mediated by cell–cell junctional interactions through E-cadherin.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Fate segregation effects are additionally mediated by cell–cell junctional interactions through E-cadherin.
source: These data therefore demonstrate that TGFβ only partially regulates fate segregation and that these effects are additionally mediated by cell–cell junctional interactions through E-cadherin.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Finite element modeling predicts peak stresses of 150 Pa at the periphery of the active layer.
source: We observed peak stresses of 150 Pa at the periphery of the active layer (Figure 4B), in agreement with previous simulations (Nelson et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FEM simulation in Figure 4B.

claim: Traction stresses are collected at the periphery of patterns on both 30 kPa and 4 kPa substrates.
source: Next, we used TFM to obtain experimental measurements in liver progenitor cells, observing that traction stresses are collected at the periphery of patterns on both 30 kPa and 4 kPa substrates (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 4C.

claim: The peak magnitude and distribution of stresses across the patterns do not vary with ligand presentation.
source: The peak magnitude and distribution of stresses across the patterns did not vary with ligand presentation (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 4D.

claim: Notch signaling is not upstream of traction stress generation at the periphery.
source: TFM measurements of cells treated with GSI showed that Notch signaling was not upstream of traction stress generation at the periphery (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inhibition of TGFβ by treatment with SB-431542 results in more uniform traction stress distributions in cells presented with both IgG and DLL4.
source: In contrast, inhibition of TGFβ by treatment with SB-431542 resulted in more uniform traction stress distributions in cells presented with both IgG and DLL4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Treatment with DECMA results in more uniform traction stress distribution in cells presented with IgG but not DLL4.
source: Intriguingly, treatment with functional antibody against E-cadherin (DECMA) resulted in more uniform traction stress distribution in cells presented with IgG but not DLL4, indicating that ligand presentation in the context of reduced cell–cell interactions induces cell-generated traction stresses.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ligand presentation in the context of reduced cell–cell interactions induces cell-generated traction stresses.
source: Intriguingly, treatment with functional antibody against E-cadherin (DECMA) resulted in more uniform traction stress distribution in cells presented with IgG but not DLL4, indicating that ligand presentation in the context of reduced cell–cell interactions induces cell-generated traction stresses.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the DECMA TFM data.

claim: Mechanical stresses are collected at the periphery, coincident with peripheral biliary fate.
source: In sum, these data show that mechanical stresses are collected at the periphery, coincident with peripheral biliary fate, and are further dependent on TGFβ signaling and E-cadherin interactions between cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Mechanical stresses are dependent on TGFβ signaling and E-cadherin interactions between cells.
source: In sum, these data show that mechanical stresses are collected at the periphery, coincident with peripheral biliary fate, and are further dependent on TGFβ signaling and E-cadherin interactions between cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Concentration profiles of Notch receptor and repressor in models including trans-activation and steeper stress gradients are qualitatively consistent with experimental data.
source: Concentration profiles of Notch receptor and repressor, a measure of Notch signaling activity, in models including trans-activation and steeper stress gradients were also qualitatively consistent with our experimental data (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by computational modeling in Figure 5B.

claim: Simulations without stress suggest a biphasic distribution of receptor, which was not observed experimentally.
source: Notably, simulations without stress suggested a biphasic distribution of receptor, which we did not observe experimentally.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on comparison of simulation and experimental data.

claim: Treatment with blebbistatin reduces peripheral OPN+ cell percentages.
source: As experimental validation, we treated cells with blebbistatin (Figure 5C), an inhibitor of myosin II ATPases, and observed reduced peripheral OPN+ cell percentages (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling and quantification in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Blebbistatin treatment results in loss of peripheral traction stresses.
source: TFM measurements obtained in parallel indicated loss of peripheral traction stresses in cells treated with blebbistatin (Figure 5D), in agreement with the known action of this inhibitor.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 5D.

claim: A simple model of Notch trans-activation coupled with an external stress gradient is consistent with experimental findings.
source: These simulations demonstrate that a simple model of Notch trans-activation coupled with an external stress gradient is consistent with our experimental findings.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the computational modeling.

claim: FR180204 treatment reduces OPN+ cell percentages at the outer edge of the patterned domains.
source: We observed that FR180204 reduced OPN+ cell percentages at the outer edge of the patterned domains (Figure 6B), which is in accordance with our previous studies suggesting involvement of ERK in biliary differentiation (Kourouklis et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 6B.

claim: Inhibition of ROCK results in increased peripheral OPN+ cell percentages extending centrally.
source: In contrast, inhibition of ROCK resulted in increased peripheral OPN+ cell percentages extending centrally (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling and quantification in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Y-27632 treatment results in loss of peripheral traction stresses.
source: Consistent with the respective functions of the proteins targeted by these inhibitors, TFM measurements indicated loss of peripheral traction stresses in cells treated with Y-27632 but not FR180204 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 6C.

claim: FR180204 treatment does not result in loss of peripheral traction stresses.
source: Consistent with the respective functions of the proteins targeted by these inhibitors, TFM measurements indicated loss of peripheral traction stresses in cells treated with Y-27632 but not FR180204 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TFM data in Figure 6C.

claim: Inhibition of ERK signaling results in direct reduction in expression of both Jag1 and Notch2.
source: Analysis of Jag1 and Notch2 mRNA expression in cells treated with FR180204 indicated that inhibition of ERK signaling results in direct reduction in expression of both ligand and receptor (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in situ hybridization in Figure 6D.

claim: YAP exhibits increased expression at the periphery of arrayed patterns on both 30 kPa and 4 kPa substrates.
source: Furthermore, we observed that the Hippo pathway effector YAP exhibited increased expression at the periphery of arrayed patterns on both 30 kPa and 4 kPa substrates (Figure 6E), though the expression of YAP was not altered by the presence of Notch ligands in the arrayed domains (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 6E.

claim: The expression of YAP is not altered by the presence of Notch ligands in the arrayed domains.
source: Furthermore, we observed that the Hippo pathway effector YAP exhibited increased expression at the periphery of arrayed patterns on both 30 kPa and 4 kPa substrates (Figure 6E), though the expression of YAP was not altered by the presence of Notch ligands in the arrayed domains (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Peripheral YAP expression suggests a potential role for the Hippo pathway in progenitor fate segregation.
source: This observation of peripheral YAP expression is especially interesting in light of recent findings regarding the demonstrated role of YAP in biliary fate (Yimlamai et al., 2014) and suggests a potential role for the Hippo pathway in progenitor fate segregation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of peripheral YAP expression and prior literature.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on myosin-mediated cell contractility and ERK signaling.
source: Collectively, these data show that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on myosin-mediated cell contractility and ERK signaling and is decoupled from mechanical stress when ROCK is inhibited.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Peripheral biliary differentiation is decoupled from mechanical stress when ROCK is inhibited.
source: Collectively, these data show that peripheral biliary differentiation is dependent on myosin-mediated cell contractility and ERK signaling and is decoupled from mechanical stress when ROCK is inhibited.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Only shJag1 cells exhibit loss of peripheral SOX9 expression.
source: In agreement with the data for OPN, only shJag1 cells exhibited loss of peripheral SOX9 expression (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 7D.

claim: Knockdown of both Jag1 and Dll1 results in decreased central HNF4A expression.
source: Interestingly, knockdown of both Jag1 and Dll1 resulted in decreased central HNF4A expression (Figure 7B and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunolabeling in Figure 7B and D.

claim: Ligand knockdown does not reduce cell-generated traction stresses compared to control cells.
source: TFM of shJag1 and shDll1 cells showed no reduction in cell-generated traction stresses by ligand knockdown compared to control cells (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: Dll1 has an unanticipated function of antagonizing biliary fate.
source: These data establish contrasting roles for Jag1 and Dll1 in biliary differentiation in which Dll1 has the unanticipated function of antagonizing biliary fate and, further, suggest that the ligands are involved in hepatocytic differentiation of progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Jag1 and Dll1 are involved in hepatocytic differentiation of progenitor cells.
source: These data establish contrasting roles for Jag1 and Dll1 in biliary differentiation in which Dll1 has the unanticipated function of antagonizing biliary fate and, further, suggest that the ligands are involved in hepatocytic differentiation of progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results based on the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Cell contractility is a key inducer of biliary fate in liver progenitors.
source: We show in this work that cell contractility is a key inducer of biliary fate in liver progenitors and elaborate roles for cell–cell interactions and mechanotransduction pathway activity in addition to established regulation by Notch and TGFβ signaling.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Increased cytoskeletal tension in hepatocytes may lead to transcriptional and epigenetic repression of HNF4A.
source: These findings are consistent with other recent efforts toward delineating the impact of substrate stiffness on hepatocyte function, which have identified potential mechanisms of transcriptional and epigenetic repression of HNF4A in hepatocytes experiencing increased cytoskeletal tension (Desai et al., 2016; Cozzolino et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The divergence in fate trajectories with blebbistatin and Y-27632 treatment may be due to the antagonism of ROCK against RAC1-induced adherens-junction formation.
source: It is possible this divergence is due to the antagonism of ROCK against RAC1-induced adherens-junction formation (Wildenberg et al., 2006), suggesting that increased cell–cell interactions in the context of reduced cytoskeletal tension is supportive of biliary fate.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Increased cell–cell interactions in the context of reduced cytoskeletal tension is supportive of biliary fate.
source: It is possible this divergence is due to the antagonism of ROCK against RAC1-induced adherens-junction formation (Wildenberg et al., 2006), suggesting that increased cell–cell interactions in the context of reduced cytoskeletal tension is supportive of biliary fate.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion.

claim: Notch ligand–receptor binding may be dependent on adherens junction formation.
source: Further evidence for this hypothesis is our observation of uniform induction of biliary fate by DLL4 presentation in cells with adherens junctions inhibited by DECMA (Figure 3), results which raise the additional possibility that Notch ligand–receptor binding is dependent on adherens junction formation.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion based on the DECMA data.

claim: Delta ligand expression promotes cell–cell interactions independent of adherens junction formation in human keratinocytes.
source: Lowell et al. provide evidence of such a mechanism in human keratinocytes, observing mutual exclusion of E-cadherin and Delta ligand and further noting that ligand expression promotes cell–cell interactions independent of adherens junction formation (Lowell et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: TGFβ signaling is not the single factor responsible for peripheral biliary fate and associated gradient formation.
source: It is therefore not likely that TGFβ signaling is the single factor responsible for peripheral biliary fate and associated gradient formation, though it may act through autocrine or paracrine regulation to enable differentiation by other mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference in the discussion based on the SB-431542 data.

claim: TGFβ may act through autocrine or paracrine regulation to enable differentiation by other mechanisms.
source: It is therefore not likely that TGFβ signaling is the single factor responsible for peripheral biliary fate and associated gradient formation, though it may act through autocrine or paracrine regulation to enable differentiation by other mechanisms.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion.

claim: TGFβ serves as a leading signal in the biphasic activation of HEY1 via interactions with SMAD3 and SMAD4 transcriptional regulators, whereas the lagging signal consists of sustained HEY1-mediated activation of JAG1 signaling dependent on ERK.
source: For instance, Zavadil et al. showed that TGFβ serves as a leading signal in the biphasic activation of HEY1 via interactions with SMAD3 and SMAD4 transcriptional regulators, whereas the lagging signal consisted of sustained HEY1-mediated activation of JAG1 signaling dependent on ERK (Zavadil et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: In the context of liver progenitor fate, the biphasic TGFβ-Notch model would require only moderate amounts of autocrine TGFβ to activate the Notch transcriptional machinery leading to ligand expression and associated biliary differentiation.
source: In the context of liver progenitor fate, this model would require only moderate amounts of autocrine TGFβ to activate the Notch transcriptional machinery leading to ligand expression and associated biliary differentiation.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion based on the cited model.

claim: YAP may serve as a mechanistic effector downstream of peripherally-induced cytoskeletal tension in progenitor cells.
source: Last, our observation of peripherally-expressed cytoplasmic YAP (Figure 6) is intriguing in light of recent literature regarding the role of YAP as a mechanosensor (Dupont et al., 2011) and regulator of liver cell fate (Yimlamai et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2016) and might serve as a mechanistic effector downstream of peripherally-induced cytoskeletal tension in progenitor cells.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion based on the YAP data and prior literature.

claim: TFM of progenitor cells treated with GSI places generation of traction stresses prior to Notch-mediated biliary differentiation.
source: TFM of progenitor cells treated with GSI places generation of traction stresses prior to Notch-mediated biliary differentiation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the TFM data.

claim: TFM of cells treated with SB-431542 provides evidence that TGFβ is upstream of traction stress.
source: In contrast, TFM of cells treated with SB-431542 provides evidence that TGFβ is upstream of traction stress (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), in accordance with the biphasic model described above in which TGFβ serves as an initial stimulus to Notch activity as well as potential feed-forward induction of cell contractility by TGFβ under conditions of mechanical stress (Tomasek et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the TFM data and prior literature.

claim: TGFβ may induce feed-forward induction of cell contractility under conditions of mechanical stress.
source: In contrast, TFM of cells treated with SB-431542 provides evidence that TGFβ is upstream of traction stress (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), in accordance with the biphasic model described above in which TGFβ serves as an initial stimulus to Notch activity as well as potential feed-forward induction of cell contractility by TGFβ under conditions of mechanical stress (Tomasek et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Ligand–intermediate filament interactions may provide a mechanism linking cytoskeletal stress and Notch.
source: Recent descriptions of new modes of non-canonical Notch signaling provide other potential mechanisms linking cytoskeletal stress and Notch through ligand–intermediate filament interactions (Antfolk et al., 2017) or Notch transmembrane domain-mediated activation of RAC1 signaling (Polacheck et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Notch transmembrane domain-mediated activation of RAC1 signaling may provide a mechanism linking cytoskeletal stress and Notch.
source: Recent descriptions of new modes of non-canonical Notch signaling provide other potential mechanisms linking cytoskeletal stress and Notch through ligand–intermediate filament interactions (Antfolk et al., 2017) or Notch transmembrane domain-mediated activation of RAC1 signaling (Polacheck et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The introduction of mechanical stress as a positive regulator of Notch receptor and Notch ligand expression is sufficient to generate a patterning response with enhanced peripheral Notch activation.
source: The results of this integrated model demonstrate that the introduction of mechanical stress as a positive regulator of Notch receptor and Notch ligand expression is sufficient to generate a patterning response with enhanced peripheral Notch activation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the computational modeling results.

claim: The presence of DLL4 in the arrayed domains appears to enhance central expression of Jag1 and Notch2 mRNA on 30 kPa but not 4 kPa substrates.
source: Notably from the in situ hybridization experiments, the presence of the Notch ligand DLL4 in the arrayed domains appeared to enhance central expression of Jag1 and Notch2 mRNA on 30 kPa but not 4 kPa substrates (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the in situ hybridization data.

claim: Central expression of Notch pathway components may not be sufficient for biliary differentiation.
source: However, cells presented with DLL4 on 30 kPa substrates exhibited preferential biliary differentiation at the periphery with minimal biliary differentiation centrally, indicating that central expression of Notch pathway components may not be sufficient for biliary differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference in the discussion based on the comparison of mRNA expression and differentiation patterns.

claim: The spatial distribution of mechanical stress signals may impact cell differentiation not only by influencing the expression of Notch pathway members but also through interactions with downstream Notch-mediated transcription or through cooperation with TGFβ and ERK.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that the spatial distribution of mechanical stress signals may impact cell differentiation not only by influencing the expression of Notch pathway members but also through interactions with downstream Notch-mediated transcription or through cooperation with TGFβ and ERK, which is required for differentiation.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The reduction of central HNF4A with knockdown of either Jag1 or Dll1 suggests a role for cell–cell interactions with ligand-presenting cells in hepatocytic differentiation.
source: The reduction of central HNF4A with knockdown of either ligand is particularly interesting and suggests a role for cell–cell interactions with ligand-presenting cells in hepatocytic differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference in the discussion based on the knockdown data.

claim: The loss of biliary differentiation with Jag1 knockdown is consistent with the known role of Jag1 expressed in the mesenchyme of the portal vein.
source: The loss of biliary differentiation with Jag1 knockdown is consistent with the known role of Jag1 expressed in the mesenchyme of the portal vein (Hofmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Dll1 has a cell-intrinsic inhibitory role in biliary differentiation in contrast with that of Jag1.
source: The unanticipated increase in OPN+ cells as a consequence of Dll1 knockdown, however, has fewer precedents and suggests an cell-intrinsic inhibitory role in contrast with that of Jag1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the knockdown data.

claim: The differential cell-extrinsic activity of the ligands might be explained in part by the known preferential affinity of ligands for specific receptors.
source: The differential cell-extrinsic activity of the ligands might be explained in part by the known preferential affinity of ligands for specific receptors (Yamamoto et al., 2012; Andrawes et al., 2013) as well as recent evidence showing that DLL4 binds Notch receptors with greater affinity and requires less mechanical tension to activate signaling (Luca et al., 2017).
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Substrate stiffness alters the baseline levels of hepatocyte and biliary markers, with stiffer substrates promoting biliary differentiation and reducing hepatocyte differentiation.
source: Although substrate stiffness did not substantially influence mechanical stress profiles as measured by TFM (Figure 4), substrate stiffness altered the baseline levels of hepatocyte and biliary markers, with stiffer substrates promoting biliary differentiation and reducing hepatocyte differentiation (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the experimental data.

claim: With decreasing pattern diameter, a greater fraction of the cells are at the periphery and exhibit biliary differentiation.
source: Our analysis of different pattern sizes suggested that peripheral differentiation was independent of diameter (Figure 1—figure supplement 3). As a result, with decreasing diameter, a greater fraction of the cells are at the periphery and exhibit biliary differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the pattern size data.

claim: The structure of the portal vein may play a role in defining the geometric and mechanical cues presented to the nascent biliary cells during liver development.
source: Interestingly, during liver development, biliary differentiation is initiated as a ductal plate consisting of a layer of differentiating progenitor cells that encircle the portal vein (Ober and Lemaigre, 2018). Based on our findings related to the spatial patterning of progenitor differentiation, it is reasonable to hypothesize that the structure of the portal vein may play a role in defining the geometric and mechanical cues presented to the nascent biliary cells.
evidence: This is speculation in the discussion based on the experimental findings and developmental context.

source: In these studies, we utilized BMEL cells, which are untransformed and have been demonstrated to exhibit bipotential differentiation both in vitro and in vivo (Strick-Marchand and Weiss, 2002; Strick-Marchand et al., 2004).

claim: The mechanoresponsiveness of liver progenitors has crucial implications not only for development but also disease.

claim: Cholangiocytic cells derived from transitional progenitors have been implicated in the pathogenesis of cholangiopathies, cholangiocarcinomas, and related disorders through compensatory ductular reactions.
source: Cholangiocytic cells derived from transitional progenitors have been implicated in the pathogenesis of cholangiopathies, cholangiocarcinomas, and related disorders through compensatory ductular reactions (Gouw et al., 2011) and are further thought to play a role in regenerating the liver by transdifferentiation (Boulter et al., 2012; He et al., 2014; Raven et al., 2017).

claim: The mechanisms described in this work may contribute to early sensing of and differentiation responses to the stiff, fibrotic microenvironments in both ductular reactions and regeneration.
source: The mechanisms we describe here may contribute to early sensing of and differentiation responses to the stiff, fibrotic microenvironments in both ductular reactions and regeneration, contributing to the biliary fates observed in these contexts.
